title: THE UNCLE’S REQUEST
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! Berlin-based Afro-Cuban director Ricardo Bacallao is also the writer of this original thriller. Combining an assassination plot with dysfunctional family dynamics driven by hardline exile politics, THE UNCLE’S REQUEST was shot entirely in New York City.

title: Late Fame
description: In Kent Jones’s marvelously witty second feature, a once-upon-a-time New York poet (Willem Dafoe) gets an ego boost when he is welcomed into the world of an emerging literary salon, but must reckon with the authenticity of his newfound circle of twentysomething admirers.

title: The Peril at Pincer Point
description: Dispatched to a fog-shrouded isle on a mission to gather audio “unprecedented in film history,” a sound recordist stumbles upon a mysterious missing person’s case that may or may not have something to do with spooky local rumors of a phantom sea captain.

title: Sound and Fury presents HOLE DWELLER, DIPLODOCUS & GARGOYLE
KYOKO KAGAWA RARITIES: LITTLE PEACH / ANZUKKO
description: This summer Anthology, Asia Society, and The Japan Foundation, New York, join forces for a celebration of the career of actress Kyoko Kagawa, who for the past 75 years has been one of the shining lights of Japanese cinema, delivering indelible performances in films by Mikio Naruse, Yasujiro Ozu, Kenji Mizoguchi, Kozaburo Yoshimura, Akira Kurosawa, Ishiro Honda, Hirokazu Kore-eda, and many others. The five-film series, “Kyoko Kagawa Rarities”, begins with an opening night screening at Anthology, before continuing uptown at Asia Society for the following three days. The opening night event features an exceedingly rare screening of Mikio Naruse’s LITTLE PEACH, described by Chris Fujiwara as both “a masterpiece of Naruse’s elliptical and unemphatic fifties style” and “one of the harshest of Naruse’s female melodramas.” Known for her iconic roles as the little sister or the enduring daughter, Kagawa here lends her tenderness to the beleaguered adult role of wife to a would-be novelist in perpetual collapse. Echoing SOUND OF THE MOUNTAIN in the many walks and talks with the great Sō Yamamura as paternal figure, with its buoyant bike rides and painful vision of marriage as social fate, the film also gestures at a spiritual afterlife for Ozu’s LATE SPRING. Following this opening night event, “Kyoko Kagawa Rarities” continues at Asia Society through Sunday, August 16, with screenings of FAREWELL TO THE HIGHLAND STATION (Nobuo Nakagawa, 1951), TOKYO RENDEZVOUS (Chihiro Ikeda, 2008), FIVE SISTERS (Seiji Hisamatsu, 1954), and SHOZO, A CAT AND TWO WOMEN (Shiro Toyoda, 1956), featuring imported archival prints and newly translated subtitles. “Kyōko Kagawa Rarities” is programmed by Joseph Eusebio and Akinaru Rokkaku and is a co-presentation of Asia Society, Anthology Film Archives, and The Japan Foundation, New York. For more info about the Asia Society screenings visit: https://asiasociety.org/new-york/kyoko-kagawa-rarities Special thanks to Hiroyuki Kojima (Japan Foundation, New York), Inney Prakash (Asia Society), and Shion Komatsu (Toho).

title: Fatal Attraction
description: Adrian Lyne’s groundbreaking 1987 erotic thriller, which garnered six Oscar nominations, contributed to the phenomenal boom of this subgenre, and it remains iconic and timeless. Glenn Close is compelling in her portrayal of Alex, a book editor who has an affair with Dan (Michael Douglas), a happily married attorney whose life becomes an unbearable torture after the tryst. Passion turns into obsession; Alex not only terrorizes Dan but also his wife and young daughter. Close’s deep dive into Alex’s psychological state, exhibited in the extreme measures she takes to possess Dan, is manifested in an intense performance,and the chemistry she shares with Douglas’s riveting Dan creates simultaneously repulsive and magnetic dynamics between them.

title: My Dinner with Andre             / Vanya on 42nd Street

Playing variations on their own New York–honed personas, Shawn and Gregory, who also cowrote the screenplay, dive in with introspective intellectual gusto, and Malle captures it all with a delicate, artful detachment. A fascinating freeze-frame of cosmopolitan culture, My Dinner with André remains a unique work in cinema history. (Janus Films)

title: CÓDIGO MARCOS
description: A highly personal look at Rosario Suárez, the former prima ballerina of the Ballet Nacional de Cuba, an expressive dancer with a dazzling technique and a singular interpretive style.
director: Patricia Pérez Fernández and Liena Cid Navia

title: Late Fame
description: In Kent Jones’s marvelously witty second feature, a once-upon-a-time New York poet (Willem Dafoe) gets an ego boost when he is welcomed into the world of an emerging literary salon, but must reckon with the authenticity of his newfound circle of twentysomething admirers.

title: Cam
description: Director Daniel Goldhaber and screenwriter Isa Mazzei anticipated our present moment with razor-sharp prescience in their first collaboration, an unnerving fable about a camgirl’s harrowing fight to wrest back control of her online persona from an invisible adversary.

title: TWIN PEAKS: THE RETURN Parts 17 & 18
description: The American Cinematheque is a member-donor-volunteer supported 501(c)(3) non-profit arts organization whose mission is to celebrate the experience of cinema.

title: THE EMIGRANT
description: One of director Youssef Chahine’s most controversial works ignited a firestorm of criticism from both Islamic and Christian voices, who objected to its liberal reinterpretation of the biblical story of Joseph (here renamed Ram to skirt censorship that forbids the depiction of religious figures). Nevertheless the film proved one of Chahine’s biggest commercial triumphs at home, a passionate evocation of ancient Egypt that uses the story—in which a young dreamer (Khaled el-Nabawy) leaves behind his backwards rural home and sets off to the intellectual center of Egypt on a journey fraught with political and sexual peril—to comment on deeply personal ideas about resistance, sacrifice, and liberation.

title: Les Bonnes Femmes
description: An early and enormous artistic triumph of the French New Wave, Chabrol’s quietly class-conscious film records the dreams, dramas, and self-deceptions of a quartet of young Parisian girls working at an appliance shop, among them Bernadette Lafont and Stéphane Audran. A study of the social habits of the petite bourgeoisie, set against indubitably authentic locations seen in crisp black-and-white courtesy DP Henri Decaë, which develops into a melancholy cautionary tale on the risks of romantic illusion. Part of Among Friends

title: The Warriors
description: “Waaarriors! Come out and play-ay!” Falsely accused of responsibility for the assassination of New York’s most powerful ganglord during a citywide summit in the Bronx’s Van Cortlandt Park, Swan (Michael Beck) and his fellow Warriors now have to fight their way back, block by block and mano a mano, to the safe shores of their Coney Island turf. The film’s knuckle-busting action choreography and its vision of NYC as a coliseum-like proving grounds for epic heroism—its source, at a distance, is Xenophon’s 4th century BC Anabasis—are delectable, but its greatness lies in its attention to character, how it lets us see a crew of provincial Brooklynites gradually discovering they’re the toughest dudes in town. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: La Notte
description: Novelist Giovanni Pontano (Marcello Mastroianni) is the toast of the Italian literary scene, but smothered by the trappings of success. His misery weighs heavily on his wife, Lidia (Jeanne Moreau), already carrying her own cargo of existential anguish. In the course of a day and a night—spent at a hospital sickroom, a book launch, a nightclub, and a party at an industrialist’s villa, where Giovanni flirts extensively with the host’s daughter, Valentina (Monica Vitti)—the couple must come to terms with the extinction of the love that once existed between them… or not? A film steeped in despair but thrilling in its adventurous, architectonic use of the cinematic medium, from its opening credits—an avant-jazz/musique concrète overture accompanying the industrialized Milanese cityscape—to its beguiling final scene. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: TAKE ME TO TOWN
description: A pretty saloon entertainer escapes the marshal’s custody and hides in a small town where she unexpectedly becomes surrogate mother to three motherless boys who wish to see their father re-married.

title: Deliverance
description: A quartet of city slicker businessman buddies (Jon Voight, Ned Beatty, Ronny Cox and, in a star-making role, Burt Reynolds) leave Atlanta to head into the Georgia backwoods for what’s meant to be a little weekend canoe trip… and stumble headlong instead into the hidden horrors lurking in the old Southland. The trial-by-fire endurance test that they’ll pass through makes for pure, pulse-pounding cinema, with at least three scenes—the “Dueling Banjos” gas station stop, Beatty’s “Squeal like a pig!” humiliation, and the white-water rapids set piece—that rank above the most remembered in ’70s American cinema. Part of Going Up the Country

title: The Invite
description: Does your summer need a little spice? Have we got the dinner party for you! Join us in the microcinema for Olivia Wilde’s wildly entertaining and perversely hilarious comedy The Invite for a fun and naughty night of indie cinema! Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

title: QUEEN OF THURSDAYS / LA REINA DE LOS JUEVES
description: A highly personal look at Rosario Suárez, the former prima ballerina of the Ballet Nacional de Cuba, an expressive dancer with a dazzling technique and a singular interpretive style. Followed by a Q&A with protagonist Rosario Suárez!

title: Nil by Mouth
description: Set in the hardscrabble South London of the filmmaker’s own youth and dedicated—in a more than slightly ambivalent gesture—to the memory of his father, Gary Oldman’s disarmingly raw debut as writer/director/producer flings us into a working-class family’s lives of profane squabbling and substance abuse as lived in the pressure cooker of a council estate flat: tyrannical father Ray (Ray Winstone); long-suffering wife, Val (Kathy Burke); Val’s junkie brother, Billy (Charlie Creed-Miles); Val’s mother and grandmother (Oldman’s sister, billed as Laila Morse, and Edna Doré); and the couple’s young daughter, who has no choice but to soak in the ambient trauma of her surroundings. “Unflinching and observant… There is humor in it, and tender insight… We sense Oldman’s ability to understand, if not forgive.” —Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times Part of Gary Oldman: The Protean Man

title: BLACK GOD, WHITE DEVIL / DEUS E O DIABO NA TERRA DO SOL
description: Glauber Rocha’s sophomore feature is a scorched-earth allegory about the blind followers of dead-end ideologies. Somewhere in the Brazilian hinterlands of the 1940s, ranch hand Manoel becomes an outlaw after killing his swindling boss. He pledges allegiance to Sebastião, a self-styled holy man who preaches revolt against rich landowners even as he perpetrates unspeakable acts of violent zealotry against the innocent. While the landowners hire a mercenary to take out Sebastião, Manoel and his wife Rosa join cangaceiros Corisco and Dadá, only to find themselves once more in league with evil, deluded forces. Steeped in history, myth, religion, and politics, and suffused with the feverish intensity of the blistering desert, BLACK GOD, WHITE DEVIL is one of the Cinema Novo movement’s most uncompromising statements on current social issues as well as the universal problem of mindless fanaticism.

title: Walkabout
description: Having fled into the Outback after their father has a psychotic episode that threatens their very lives, two Sydney-bred adolescent siblings (Jenny Agutter and Luc Roeg, the director’s son) meet an Aboriginal teenager (David Gulpilil, in his debut role) on his traditional “walkabout”—a rite-of-passage journey, undertaken in solitude—who aids them in adjusting to the apparently harsh, unforgiving landscape around them, a landscape that, as Walkabout progresses, is heavily romanticised, revealing an Edenic splendor lurking beneath its sun-baked surface. A foundational text of the Australian New Wave and a film of genuinely awe-striking natural beauty, shot by cinematographer-turned-director Roeg himself. Part of Going Up the Country

title: Goody Goody
description: A mom-to-be’s stubborn conviction that she alone knows what’s best for her unborn child is put to the gruesomest of tests when alarming complications arise during a home delivery in director Raymond Creamer’s diabolical spin on prenatal horror.

title: Magic Mike
description: Is it hot in here, or is it just Matt Bomer? Get ready to go wild with Mike and the boys in the original thirst trap throwdown! Would anyone have guessed that Steven Soderbergh would have taken on the male-exotic dance scene with such zeal? With Channing Tatum and a cavalcade of the sexiest men in America stripping down to their skivvies, it’s no wonder this beefcake bonanza launched the thirst of millions worldwide and led to a jock-thrusting empire that anyone can get behind! You can leave your dollar bills at home, we’ve got the money gun prepped and primed for this sexy fun night for anyone who’s feeling a little thirsty with all this heat!

title: Doughboys Present IN & OUT
description: Hosts and longtime frenemies Mike Mitchell and Nick Wiger review chain restaurants and bicker about absolutely everything on the iHeartRadio award-winning Best Food Podcast, Doughboys .

title: The Invite
description: Does your summer need a little spice? Have we got the dinner party for you! Join us in the microcinema for Olivia Wilde’s wildly entertaining and perversely hilarious comedy The Invite for a fun and naughty night of indie cinema! Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

title: Cabaret (IB Tech Print)
description: Winner of 8 Academy Awards, including Best Actress and Best Director, director / choreographer Bob Fosse’s adaptation of the Broadway show is a stylish, big screen musical masterpiece. Set in 1931 Berlin, Cabaret chronicles young American Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) and her bohemian life as a performer at the Kit Kat Klub during the last days of the Weimar Republic, as well as her relationships with a reserved academic (Michael York) and a rich playboy (Helmut Griem). Minnelli is electric in her star-making role and a stellar Joel Grey shines in his Best Supporting Actor performance as the bawdy Master of Ceremonies.

title: CAM & FACES OF DEATH + Q&A w/ Daniel Goldhaber & Isa Mazzei
description: CAM and FACES OF DEATH come together for a special double feature, followed by an in-person Q&A with director Daniel Goldhaber and writer Isa Mazzei.

title: Unfaithful
description: Diane Lane received an Oscar nomination for her remarkable portrayal of Connie Sumner, who lives an admirable life in an upper-class neighborhood of upstate New York with loving husband Edward and 8-year-old son Charlie. In a gush of wind, an unpredictable encounter occurs between Connie and an attractive man in the street of New York City, followed by the irreversible measures of an illicit affair. Adrian Lyne candidly and without judgment surveys on lust, passion, jealousy, and guilt, unearthing a dark, dense pool of human emotion and the arbitrariness of its motivation.

title: DANIEL CHILE + RICARDO VEGA
description: Daniel Chile THE LAST GAME / EL ÚLTIMO JUEGO 2026, 24 min, DCP. In Spanish with English subtitles. New York Premiere! A children’s game turns into something sinister and violent, probing the extremes of human behavior amidst a dystopian reality. Ricardo Vega I LOVE YOU AND I’LL TAKE YOU TO THE MOVIES / TE QUIERO Y TE LLEVO AL CINE 1993, 60 min, DCP. In Spanish with English subtitles. Acclaimed for its loose structure, and virtually absent of dialogue, this experimental film focuses on the lives of three young people in 1980s Havana, exploring themes of doubt, fear, and the search for meaning through three related stories. Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: The Hunger
description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit assistance from Susan Sarandon’s geriatrics researcher, then find themselves in a very, very attractive throuple. Yes, that’s “Bela Lugosi’s Dead” artists Bauhaus in a brief cameo. “Twenty years after Belle de Jour, Saint Laurent once again dressed Catherine Deneuve, for Tony Scott’s cult 1980s tale of elegant vampires. Her shoulder pads, lipstick, and veils defined an era.” —David Campany, Creative Director, International Center of Photography Part of Dressed by Yves Saint Laurent

title: Obsession
description: De Palma’s twisted twist on Hitchcock’s Vertigo stars Cliff Robertson as a wealthy New Orleans real-estate developer still mourning the loss of his beloved wife (Dead Ringers’ Genevieve Bujold) and daughter years after their abductions until, on a visit to Florence, he encounters her exact double. (In addition to Hitch, screenwriter Paul Schrader drew inspiration from Dante and his infatuation with muse Beatrice.) With lusciously gauzy cinematography by Vilmos Zsigmond, a richly romantic score by Hitch regular Bernard Herrmann, and Big Easy Baroque location shooting, this is moviemaking as ultrarich confection, a swooning transport “to a more romantic era… and the simple, touching pleasures denied the audience by the current antiromantic spirit of the movies” [Richard Schickel]. Part of In Her Shadow

title: The Weed Eaters
description: The munchies and murder don’t mix… or do they? Chaos and cannibalism ensue when four stoner friends discover a peculiar strain of weed at the middle-of-nowhere rental property where they’ve decamped for a toked-out New Year’s retreat.

title: CEMETERY WITHOUT CROSSES / UNE CORDE…UN COLT…
description: After her husband is lynched by bandits, Michèle Mercier seeks revenge and turns to an old friend for help (played by star/creator Robert Hossein of RIFIFI). A solitary figure who lives in a ghost town and dons a single black glove before each gunfight, Hossein soon infiltrates the widow’s enemies to force a showdown. This is a French take on the Italians’ take on American genres – a “baguette western.” Inspired by the international success of Sergio Leone’s DOLLARS trilogy, and armed with the catchiest of theme songs via international cult figure Scott Walker, CEMETERY WITHOUT CROSSES offers a Gallic spin on the European gunslinger genre.

title: Commando
description: Get your bazookas ready for a non-stop action bonanza as Schwarzenegger takes on an army of mercenaries to save his daughter (none other than Alyssa Milano!) by brawling in the mall, and blowing up as much of LA as he can! One of the best popcorn blockbusters of the 1980s, Rae Dawn Chong and the Governator team up for action, for fun, and for revenge in this bad-ass specatacular. John Matrix, the former leader of a special commando strike force that always got the toughest jobs done, is forced back into action when his young daughter is kidnapped by a group of assassins led by ultra villain Bennett (Vernon Wells). To find her, Matrix has to fight his way through an array of punks, killers, one of his former commandos, and a fully equipped private army. With the help of a feisty stewardess and an old friend, Matrix has only a few hours to overcome his greatest challenge: finding his daughter before she’s killed. Join us for all the fun as we watch this explosive banger big and loud!

title: Lockjaw
description: With writer/director Sabrina Greco in person at both screenings! Friday, August 14th Greco will be in conversation with Micah Gottlieb of Mezzanine Cinema and the Los Angeles Festival of Movies .

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: The Dark Knight Rises
description: Bane, an imposing terrorist, attacks Gotham City and disrupts its eight-year-long period of peace. This forces Bruce Wayne to come out of hiding and don the cape and cowl of Batman again.

title: Irreversible
description: Fourteen long sequence shots arranged in reverse chronology take us on a journey from hell to heaven, from nightmarish violence to connubial bliss. In a BDSM club evocatively called Club Rectum, Pierre (Albert Dupontel) dashes in the face of a man who’s just broken the arm of his friend, Marcus (Vincent Cassel), and is preparing to rape him. From this memorable cold open, we see the events leading up to this bloody denouement—an evening that begins (or ends, as it were) as an innocent outing by the two friends and Marcus’s girlfriend, Alex (Monica Bellucci). Not a film to leave the viewer indifferent, to put it very mildly, featuring a positively punitive, bowel-churning soundtrack by Daft Punk’s Thomas Bangalter. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: Pulp Fiction
description: Two hitmen out to retrieve a suitcase stolen. An aging boxer paid to lose his next fight. A couple of young lovers and small-time thieves who decide they need a change of venue. Their lives are woven together in the exhilarating Pulp Fiction . Quentin Tarantino’s Palme d’Or-winning classic is packed with electric dialogue, potent pop-culture touchstones, and an unforgettable ensemble cast. You won’t know the facts until you’ve seen the fiction.

title: Misbehaving Ladies
description: A princess from Europe plays along when she is mistaken for a seamstress in her American hometown.

title: Scooby Doo
description: The Mystery Inc. gang from Hanna-Barbera’s classic cartoon, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You! took their sleuthing skills to the big screen with their first live-action adventure in 2002’s Scooby-Doo . Led by ‘90s teen heartthrobs and real-life couple Freddie Prinze Jr. and Sarah Michelle Gellar as Fred and Daphne, the amateur detectives Velma (Linda Cardellini), Shaggy (Matthew Lillard) and his best friend, the cowardly, always hungry, and vocal Great Dane, Scooby-Doo, reunite to solve the mystery of ghostly happenings at the tropical resort Spooky Island. From a script co-written by James Gunn and featuring Rowan Atkinson as the eccentric resort-owner, the film was a box office success on its release and continues to have an avid following.

title: The Dark Knight
description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.” Part of Gary Oldman: The Protean Man

title: A Goofy Movie
description: Head out on a road trip of goofing proportions in this very 90s animated dad joke! An endearing modern-day story about how the lovable Goof bonds with his teenage son Max on a hilarious cross-country road trip. En route to the ol’ fishing hole, they find themselves up to their floppy ears in misadventure! A movie for the goofball in all of us featuring one of the most epically 90s animated musical sequences ever!

title: A Day in the Country + People on Sunday
description: Two slices of life from Europe entre deux guerres, and two compact masterpieces. Renoir’s featurette fragment, based on a Guy de Maupassant short story and only edited 10 years after its shoot came to a premature end, evokes the disappeared world of Belle Époque France—the world of Renoir’s father, the painter Pierre-Auguste—by describing an afternoon’s outing for two young shirt-chasers, a middle-aged Paris shopkeeper, and the shopkeeper’s susceptible-to-flattery wife and daughter. People on Sunday, made by a supergroup brain trust of future cinematic luminaries including Billy Wilder, Fred Zinnemann, Robert Siodmak, and Edgar G. Ulmer, follows a quintet of Berliners through a weekend of walks along the Wannsee, domestic squabbles, and frisky flirtation. Modest in ambition, yet they contain the world in miniature. A Day in the Country (Jean Renoir, 1946, 41 mins) People on Sunday (Robert Siodmak, Edgar G. Ulmer, 1930, 74 mins) Part of Going Up the Country
director: Robert Siodmak, Jean Renoir , Edgar G. Ulmer

title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
description: Featuring a conversation with filmmaker Sasha Waters after the August 12th screening!

title: TAKE ME TO TOWN
description: A pretty saloon entertainer escapes the marshal’s custody and hides in a small town where she unexpectedly becomes surrogate mother to three motherless boys who wish to see their father re-married.

title: Knights of the Round Table
description: All the glory and splendor of King Arthur’s court presented in massive CinemaScope! The Arthurian legend receives a lavish Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer adaptation, lusciously lensed by Freddie Young ( Lawrence of Arabia ) & Stephen Dade ( Zulu ), and featuring a stirring Miklos Rozsa score. Sir Lancelot (Robert Taylor) is sworn to serve King Arthur (Mel Ferrer), but his devotion to the queen (Ava Gardner) could provide fuel for their enemies to destroy Camelot.

title: The Weed Eaters
description: The munchies and murder don’t mix… or do they? Chaos and cannibalism ensue when four stoner friends discover a peculiar strain of weed at the middle-of-nowhere rental property where they’ve decamped for a toked-out New Year’s retreat.

title: Train to Busan
description: With the South Korean peninsula in the throes of a national disaster, travelers board the KTX, a fast a train to Busan, a city unaffected by the crisis. Among them is Seok-woo, a workaholic father traveling with his daughter. When a young woman, scuffed and dazed, gets on board, an unimaginable horror erupts in the train’s claustrophobic confines. Director Yeon Sang-ho, whose prior filmmaking comprises groundbreaking animated features, balances an upbeat, kinetic energy with solid emotional storytelling to deliver much more than just an action-driven genre film.

title: Buster Keaton Shorts Block
description: Buster rises to new heights as he sails heavenward in a balloon. He bumps into clouds and, in trying to bring down a duck, punctures the gas bag and crashes in the woods where he saves Phyllis Haver from a bear and falls in love. His courtship and the balloonatic events that follow are hilarious.

title: Two by Robb Moss
description: A pair of films from Moss, a master of first-person documentary and longtime Professor at Harvard’s Department of Art, Film, and Visual Studies, who will join Metrograph for the screening. Riverdogs is Moss’s lyrical, beautifully photographed account of a 35-day trek down the Colorado River, a paean to youth, the natural world, and a fleeting moment in the increasingly distant past. In his confessional The Tourist, Moss meditates—with a wry sense of humor—on the early years of his marriage, his failed attempts to start a family with his new wife, and the daily vicissitudes of professional life as an itinerant freelance cameraman. The Tourist (Robb Moss, 1991, 60 mins) Riverdogs (Robb Moss, 1982, 32 mins) Q&A with filmmaker Robb Moss on Saturday, August 15th

title: Deliverance
description: A quartet of city slicker businessman buddies (Jon Voight, Ned Beatty, Ronny Cox and, in a star-making role, Burt Reynolds) leave Atlanta to head into the Georgia backwoods for what’s meant to be a little weekend canoe trip… and stumble headlong instead into the hidden horrors lurking in the old Southland. The trial-by-fire endurance test that they’ll pass through makes for pure, pulse-pounding cinema, with at least three scenes—the “Dueling Banjos” gas station stop, Beatty’s “Squeal like a pig!” humiliation, and the white-water rapids set piece—that rank above the most remembered in ’70s American cinema. Part of Going Up the Country

title: Scarlet Street
description: Watch out for the double cross in Fritz Lang’s film noir classic Scarlet Street starring crime cinema’s crown prince Edward G. Robinson and the infectiously alluring Joan Bennett as the feisty femme fatale. Cashier and part-time starving artist Christopher Cross is absolutely smitten with the beautiful Kitty March. Kitty plays along, but she’s really only interested in Johnny, a two-bit crook. When Kitty and Johnny find out that art dealers are interested in Chris’s work, they con him into letting Kitty take credit for the paintings. Cross allows it because he is in love with Kitty, but his love will only let her get away with so much. A razor-sharp thriller with an abundance of artistic flourishes, plus wit and wisecracks, Scarlet Street is among Fritz Lang’s most entertaining masterpieces.

title: The Invite
description: Does your summer need a little spice? Have we got the dinner party for you! Join us in the microcinema for Olivia Wilde’s wildly entertaining and perversely hilarious comedy The Invite for a fun and naughty night of indie cinema! Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

title: VOLCANO
description: A raging volcano pushes to the surface, raining a storm of deadly fire bombs and an endless tide of white-hot lava upon the stunned city.

title: Veins
description: Fraught family dynamics make for treacherous emotional terrain during a young woman’s long-delayed visit to her childhood home, where she’s alarmed to learn that her estranged father has been dead for three days—a revelation to which her mother seems strangely indifferent.

title: MAN WITH A SHOTGUN / SHOTTOGAN NO OTOKO
description: “Samurai movies often operate similarly to westerns (part of why SEVEN SAMURAI and YOJIMBO were later remade Stateside), but rarely do you see an actual Japanese western.” –Kyle Warner, CITY ON FIRE THE MAN WITH A SHOTGUN is a high point in the first five years of director Seijun Suzuki’s career within Nikkatsu’s “Borderless Action” series. Drawing inspiration from Hollywood and the French New Wave, Suzuki’s works for Nikkatsu blended East and West, movie-fueled fantasies, and gritty realities of life in postwar Japan.

title: Jacob’s Ladder
description: After returning home from the Vietnam War, veteran Jacob Singer struggles to maintain his sanity. Plagued by hallucinations and flashbacks, Singer rapidly falls apart as the world and people around him morph and twist into disturbing images. His girlfriend, Jezzie, and ex-wife, Sarah, try to help, but to little avail. Even Singer’s chiropractor friend, Louis, fails to reach him as he descends into madness.

title: THE WALKER
description: A highly engaging and dynamic exploration of artist Humberto Castro’s personal life, as well as the Neofigurative aesthetics that define his work.

title: Hannibal
description: Hopkins reprises his role from 1991’s The Silence of the Lambs as psychiatrist-turned-cannibal serial killer Hannibal Lecter in Scott’s follow-up, a gristly fairy tale that finds FBI special agent Clarice Starling (Julianne Moore, ably taking on the role originated by Jodie Foster) racing against time to find to catch up with her old foil before he’s located by Mason R. Verger (Gary Oldman), a sadistic scion of enormous wealth who, after years earlier being grotesquely mutilated by Lecter, has dedicated the entirety of his power and influence towards a terrible and extravagant dream of vengeance. Unidentified in promotional materials and unbilled until the film’s closing credits, wholly unrecognizable under a prosthetic mask, and stripped of almost every expressive tool an actor traditionally relies upon to practice their craft, Oldman offers up an indelible portrayal of utter and absolute human corruption. Part of Gary Oldman: The Protean Man

title: Nil by Mouth
description: Set in the hardscrabble South London of the filmmaker’s own youth and dedicated—in a more than slightly ambivalent gesture—to the memory of his father, Gary Oldman’s disarmingly raw debut as writer/director/producer flings us into a working-class family’s lives of profane squabbling and substance abuse as lived in the pressure cooker of a council estate flat: tyrannical father Ray (Ray Winstone); long-suffering wife, Val (Kathy Burke); Val’s junkie brother, Billy (Charlie Creed-Miles); Val’s mother and grandmother (Oldman’s sister, billed as Laila Morse, and Edna Doré); and the couple’s young daughter, who has no choice but to soak in the ambient trauma of her surroundings. “Unflinching and observant… There is humor in it, and tender insight… We sense Oldman’s ability to understand, if not forgive.” —Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times Part of Gary Oldman: The Protean Man

title: Never After Dark
description: The harrowing sixth feature from bilingual director Dave Boyle—his first shot entirely in Japan—follows a mild-mannered psychic medium who gets more than she bargained for when she accepts a job at an isolated hotel plagued by a hostile supernatural presence.

title: CEMETERY WITHOUT CROSSES / UNE CORDE…UN COLT…
description: After her husband is lynched by bandits, Michèle Mercier seeks revenge and turns to an old friend for help (played by star/creator Robert Hossein of RIFIFI). A solitary figure who lives in a ghost town and dons a single black glove before each gunfight, Hossein soon infiltrates the widow’s enemies to force a showdown. This is a French take on the Italians’ take on American genres – a “baguette western.” Inspired by the international success of Sergio Leone’s DOLLARS trilogy, and armed with the catchiest of theme songs via international cult figure Scott Walker, CEMETERY WITHOUT CROSSES offers a Gallic spin on the European gunslinger genre.

title: Lockjaw
description: With writer/director Sabrina Greco in person at both screenings! Friday, August 14th Greco will be in conversation with Micah Gottlieb of Mezzanine Cinema and the Los Angeles Festival of Movies .

title: ADIÓS CUBA
description: A female playwright explores the Cuban exodus through real-life testimonies of their experiences in countries all over the globe, including Iceland, Spain, and Angola. ADIÓS CUBA resonates strongly with today’s immigrant crisis worldwide.

title: Cabaret (IB Tech Print)
description: Winner of 8 Academy Awards, including Best Actress and Best Director, director / choreographer Bob Fosse’s adaptation of the Broadway show is a stylish, big screen musical masterpiece. Set in 1931 Berlin, Cabaret chronicles young American Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) and her bohemian life as a performer at the Kit Kat Klub during the last days of the Weimar Republic, as well as her relationships with a reserved academic (Michael York) and a rich playboy (Helmut Griem). Minnelli is electric in her star-making role and a stellar Joel Grey shines in his Best Supporting Actor performance as the bawdy Master of Ceremonies.

title: Deep Water
description: Deep Water , Adrian Lyne’s powerfully sexy, witty, and intoxicating return to the erotic thriller, finally receives its theatrical premiere. Lyne will join Hollywood Entertainment in person for a very special evening—including some unprecedented interactive surprises!

title: The Ugly
description: Starring in Yeon Sang-ho’s intimate suspense drama is Park Jeong-min, in his compelling portrayal of Dong-hwan and the younger version of his father, Yeong-gyu, in flashback sequences. Yeong-gyu, who cannot see, is a renowned wooden seal carver, respected for his intricate craftsmanship. Dong-hwan has no memory of his mother, who has been missing for 40 years—or so he’s been told—until he receives a startling call about her remains. Adapted from his own graphic novel, Yeon excavates the ugly aspects of societal standards and perceptions of beauty, and unapologetically exhibits the dark sides of human greed, desire, and trauma.

title: The Others
description: Having enjoyed a palpable international hit with his Abre Los Ojos—picked up for an American remake, under the title Vanilla Sky, by Tom Cruise—Amenábar made his English-language debut with The Others, a dolorous, deftly directed Old Dark House chiller set in the immediate aftermath of World War II, about a devoutly religious Englishwoman (Nicole Kidman, superb) living in a remote home in the Channel Island with her two young, severely photosensitive children and the strange goings-on that begin shortly after she takes on a trio of new servants. “Elegant… Creates more tension from atmosphere alone than most other horror films do from vats full of fake blood.” —The Times of London Part of In Her Shadow

title: Obsession
description: De Palma’s twisted twist on Hitchcock’s Vertigo stars Cliff Robertson as a wealthy New Orleans real-estate developer still mourning the loss of his beloved wife (Dead Ringers’ Genevieve Bujold) and daughter years after their abductions until, on a visit to Florence, he encounters her exact double. (In addition to Hitch, screenwriter Paul Schrader drew inspiration from Dante and his infatuation with muse Beatrice.) With lusciously gauzy cinematography by Vilmos Zsigmond, a richly romantic score by Hitch regular Bernard Herrmann, and Big Easy Baroque location shooting, this is moviemaking as ultrarich confection, a swooning transport “to a more romantic era… and the simple, touching pleasures denied the audience by the current antiromantic spirit of the movies” [Richard Schickel]. Part of In Her Shadow

title: BLACK GOD, WHITE DEVIL / DEUS E O DIABO NA TERRA DO SOL
description: Glauber Rocha’s sophomore feature is a scorched-earth allegory about the blind followers of dead-end ideologies. Somewhere in the Brazilian hinterlands of the 1940s, ranch hand Manoel becomes an outlaw after killing his swindling boss. He pledges allegiance to Sebastião, a self-styled holy man who preaches revolt against rich landowners even as he perpetrates unspeakable acts of violent zealotry against the innocent. While the landowners hire a mercenary to take out Sebastião, Manoel and his wife Rosa join cangaceiros Corisco and Dadá, only to find themselves once more in league with evil, deluded forces. Steeped in history, myth, religion, and politics, and suffused with the feverish intensity of the blistering desert, BLACK GOD, WHITE DEVIL is one of the Cinema Novo movement’s most uncompromising statements on current social issues as well as the universal problem of mindless fanaticism.

title: Sudden Fury
description: Brian Damude’s pitch-black, no-holds-barred Canuxploitation classic traces the sociopathic machinations of a husband who leaves his wife for dead after a car accident, angling to cash in on her inheritance.

title: The Invite
description: Does your summer need a little spice? Have we got the dinner party for you! Join us in the microcinema for Olivia Wilde’s wildly entertaining and perversely hilarious comedy The Invite for a fun and naughty night of indie cinema! Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

title: An Evening with Edgar Wright: Beyond the Valley of the Dolls
description: Our evening of epic epicness continues with a special screening of Russ Meyer’s sexy psychedelic cinematic freakout Beyond the Valley of the Dolls introduced by Edgar Wright !

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: Irreversible
description: Fourteen long sequence shots arranged in reverse chronology take us on a journey from hell to heaven, from nightmarish violence to connubial bliss. In a BDSM club evocatively called Club Rectum, Pierre (Albert Dupontel) dashes in the face of a man who’s just broken the arm of his friend, Marcus (Vincent Cassel), and is preparing to rape him. From this memorable cold open, we see the events leading up to this bloody denouement—an evening that begins (or ends, as it were) as an innocent outing by the two friends and Marcus’s girlfriend, Alex (Monica Bellucci). Not a film to leave the viewer indifferent, to put it very mildly, featuring a positively punitive, bowel-churning soundtrack by Daft Punk’s Thomas Bangalter. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: The Dark Knight Rises
description: Bane, an imposing terrorist, attacks Gotham City and disrupts its eight-year-long period of peace. This forces Bruce Wayne to come out of hiding and don the cape and cowl of Batman again.

title: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie
description: The cult Canadian show makes the giant leap to the big screen with this wildly ambitious & riotously funny instant-classic that demands to be seen with an audience. When their elaborate plans to book a show at the Rivoli goes horribly wrong, a pair of best buds (Matt Johnson & Jay McCarrol) accidentally get sent back in time to the year 2008.

title: Misbehaving Ladies
description: A princess from Europe plays along when she is mistaken for a seamstress in her American hometown.

title: Four Adventures of Reinette and Mirabelle
description: Shot quickly in and around Paris during a production break on Rohmer’s Le Rayon Vert, this breezy, witty film traces the exploits of two young women—one an ethnology student from the city, the other an unsophisticated aspiring artist from the country. Reinette and Mirabelle (played by Joëlle Miquel and Jessica Forde) become instant friends upon meeting in the first of four vignettes that make up the film (“The Blue Hour”), and in their first two days together, they decide to become roommates in Paris. Throughout the three remaining stories, they encounter many of the inevitable characters of a modern city: the impossible waiter (“The Waiter”), the Metro-station hustler (“The Beggar, the Kleptomaniac and the Hustler”), and the snooty gallery owner (“Selling the Painting”). A Metrograph Pictures release

title: The Jungle Book
description: Inspired by the adventures of the foundling Mowgli in Rudyard Kipling’s 1894 collection of the same name, The Jungle Book—the final animated Disney feature to be overseen in its production by Uncle Walt—would become one of the studio’s biggest hits, thanks in no small part to its exceptional confluence of vocal talent (yes, that’s George Sanders as the suavely sinister Bengal tiger Shere Khan) and unforgettable songbook, including perennial favorites “The Bare Necessities” and “I Wanna Be Like You (The Monkey Song),” the latter volcanically belted out by none other than jump blues howler extraordinaire Louis Prima. Brisk, breezy, and simply buckets of fun. Part of It Started With A Mouse: Hand-Drawn Classics on 35

title: Ponyo (English Dubbed)
description: Dive into this breathtaking and heartwarming adventure from the legendary Studio Ghibli, and Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki. When Sosuke, a young boy who lives on a clifftop overlooking the sea, rescues a stranded goldfish named Ponyo, he discovers more than he bargained for. Ponyo is a curious, energetic young creature who yearns to be human, but even as she causes chaos around the house, her father, a sorcerer, schemes to return Ponyo to the sea. Loosely based on Hans Christian Andersen’s classic fairy tale The Little Mermaid , Miyazaki’s breathtaking, imaginative world is brought to life with an all-star cast, featuring the voices of Cate Blanchett, Noah Cyrus, Matt Damon, Tina Fey, Frankie Jonas, Cloris Leachman, Liam Neeson, Lily Tomlin, and Betty White.

title: Walkabout
description: Having fled into the Outback after their father has a psychotic episode that threatens their very lives, two Sydney-bred adolescent siblings (Jenny Agutter and Luc Roeg, the director’s son) meet an Aboriginal teenager (David Gulpilil, in his debut role) on his traditional “walkabout”—a rite-of-passage journey, undertaken in solitude—who aids them in adjusting to the apparently harsh, unforgiving landscape around them, a landscape that, as Walkabout progresses, is heavily romanticised, revealing an Edenic splendor lurking beneath its sun-baked surface. A foundational text of the Australian New Wave and a film of genuinely awe-striking natural beauty, shot by cinematographer-turned-director Roeg himself. Part of Going Up the Country

title: Otar Iosseliani Early Shorts Program
description: A program of the inspired early shorts that established Iosseliani at the forefront of a new, rising generation of Georgian filmmakers. Featuring Akvarel, in which a quarreling working-class couple experience a revelation at an art exhibition; Sapovnela, in which an old man who tends exquisite flower gardens in the hills around Mtskheta sees his life’s work threatened by the arrival of a new road; April, in which a young couple find their happiness dwindling as their comfort increases upon moving into a brand new, squeaky clean housing development, and Tudzhi (Cast Iron), a documentary description of life in an ironworks that singles out individuals on the factory floor not as symbols of thrumming Soviet industrial might, but as human beings. Akvarel (Otar Iosseliani, 1958, 10 mins) Sapovnela (Song About a Flower) (Otar Iosseliani, 1959, 18 mins) April (Otar Iosseliani, 1962, 46 mins) Tudzhi (Cast Iron) (Otar Iosseliani, 1963, 20 mins) Part of Otar Iosseliani: Fables of Modern Life

title: Knights of the Round Table
description: All the glory and splendor of King Arthur’s court presented in massive CinemaScope! The Arthurian legend receives a lavish Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer adaptation, lusciously lensed by Freddie Young ( Lawrence of Arabia ) & Stephen Dade ( Zulu ), and featuring a stirring Miklos Rozsa score. Sir Lancelot (Robert Taylor) is sworn to serve King Arthur (Mel Ferrer), but his devotion to the queen (Ava Gardner) could provide fuel for their enemies to destroy Camelot.

title: Munich
description: After the killing of Israeli hostages at the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, a Mossad agent (Eric Bana) assembles a team to assassinate the men deemed responsible for the murders. Steven Spielberg’s fact-based international thriller is a thoughtful look at the moral costs of violence, with gripping suspense and an impressive supporting cast including Best Actor winner Geoffrey Rush ( Shine , 1996), Supporting Actor nominee Ciarán Hinds ( Belfast , 2021), and Daniel Craig, shortly before he debuted as James Bond. The film received five Oscar nominations including Best Picture, Directing, and , for John Williams’ music, his 22nd feature score for the director. Williams’s somber, restrained score focused on, in the composer’s words, “the enormous suffering and guilt, and eventually, paranoia” of Bana’s protagonist.

title: Falling Leaves
description: Iosseliani’s debut feature—winner of the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes—follows newly minted oenologists Nico and Otar, just out of winemaking school, as they head to work at an agricultural cooperative in Tbilisi, there to have their first intimate experiences of the opposite sex… as well as their introduction to the corruption bred by stifling bureaucracy and arbitrarily imposed production quotas. A stinging satire of Soviet-style economic planning and its unintended consequences smuggled within a pseudo-documentary depiction of the Georgian wine industry, and a deeply personal film about youth for the first time facing up to the full measure of adult negligence and corruption. New 4K restoration commissioned by Pastorale Productions. Part of Otar Iosseliani: Fables of Modern Life

title: Paranoid Park
description: Adapting Blake Nelson’s Y.A. novel of the same name, Van Sant renders the youth gathering place of the skate park a voluptuous dreamscape with the help of cinematographers Chris Doyle and Rain Kathy Li. Teenaged skate rat Alex—Gabe Nevins, leading a largely amateur cast recruited via MySpace—finds himself a prime suspect in the death of a security guard, silently carrying a crushing burden of knowledge through his daily rounds, a contrast to the gravity-defying liberation he finds carving it up at “Paranoid Park.” Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: A View to a Kill
description: Bond is back, and this time he’s up against Christopher Walken and the iconic Grace Jones in this Roger Moore-era 007 installment. A newly-developed microchip designed by Zorin Industries for the British Government that can survive the electromagnetic radiation caused by a nuclear explosion has landed in the hands of the KGB. James Bond must find out how and why. His suspicions soon lead him to big industry leader Max Zorin who forms a plan to destroy his only competition in Silicon Valley by triggering a massive earthquake in the San Francisco Bay.

title: THE WIND BLOWS UNDER YOUR FEET / TALPUK ALATT FÜTYÜL A SZÉL
description: “György Szomjas’s first feature – made after a decade of short documentaries – is a bold attempt at a goulash western, set on the puszta, or Great Hungarian Plain, in 1837. Mixing Miklós Jancsó imagery and a Sergio Leone narrative, this ballad-like saga opens with the image of a lone horseman on the empty plain, riding past a rude gallows. THE WIND IS WHISTLING UNDER THEIR FEET concerns the vengeful return of a legendary betyár (outlaw), briefly a hero to the local herdsmen who oppose the state building a canal across their grazing land. Although Szomjas works from ethnographic records and archival material, it is hardly surprising that this violent, primitivist film would be more popular with Hungarian audiences than critics. Replete with young guns, crooked sheriffs, tavern brawlers, and hard-bitten plug-uglies, this widescreen film is strikingly shot by Elémer Ragályi (cinematographer for most of Gyula Gazdag’s films) – a feast of loamy, autumnal colors.” –J. Hoberman

title: The Trek
description: Drawing inspiration from traditional folklore, the “Western-horror” debut feature from South African cinematographer Meekaaeel Adam is a haunting, haunted meditation on the brutal legacies of settler colonialism.

title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
description: Featuring a conversation with filmmaker Sasha Waters after the August 12th screening!

title: BEHIND MY EYES / DETRÁS DE MIS OJOS
description: The award-winning director Iván Acosta reconstructs the bitter and confusing hours following the Twin Towers attack from a video he had recorded and stashed away in a drawer.

title: There Once Was a Singing Blackbird
description: Gia (Gela Kandelaki), a timpanist in the Tbilisi Philharmonic, has made a science of getting to work just on time to hit his lone cue and then dashing out the door, so as to leave the rest of his hours open for sweet-talking women and carousing with pals. A marvelous character study of an open-handed, incurably impulsive young man infected by the bustling, on-the-go energy of the city around him, and a film that careens along with the same freewheeling spontaneity displayed by its protagonist. Screens with Georgian Ancient Songs, which Iosseliani described thusly: “It’s a film about Georgian traditional polyphony. Georgian songs are always sung in one, two, three or even four voices. It’s a story about how these songs are structured. And at the same time we show what life was like in the old days. The official reaction to the film was one of indignation. I managed to steal a print of the film and keep it safe.” Georgian Ancient Songs (Otar Ioseliani, 1969, 20 mins) Once Upon a Time There Once Was a Singing Blackbird (Otar Iosseliani, 1971, 78 mins) New 4K restoration commissioned by Pastorale Productions. Part of Otar Iosseliani: Fables of Modern Life

title: The Milk of Sorrow
description: Winner of the Golden Bear at the 59th Berlin International Film Festival, Llosa’s formidable sophomore feature focuses on Fausta (Magaly Solier, in a performance nearly free of dialogue), the only daughter of an aged Indigenous Peruvian woman who, following her mother’s death, must negotiate arrangements for her burial as well as negotiate the smothering legacy of trauma that her parent, horribly misused during the Shining Path terrorist insurgencies of the 1980s and ’90s, has left behind with her child even after herself departing this mortal coil. “Littered with unforgettable images of incongruity, destruction, and, finally, healing” [The Village Voice], The Milk of Sorrow is an exquisitely shot study in inherited injury guarded like a precious heirloom, a work of tragic magic realism. Part of In Her Shadow

title: SODA POP JOE / LIMONÁDOVÝ JOE ANEB KONSKÁ OPERA
description: “SODA POP JOE was made in 1964, during the exuberant period in Czechoslovakia filled with the hope that society was breaking free of the ideological grip of the 1950s and heading towards more freedom. The very choice of the Western and of satirical comedy was in itself already a step in opposition to the official presentation of the Western as ‘a fallen and damaging genre’. In a typical main street of a small town in the far West, a fight takes place between the handsome hero, Joe, and an ugly scoundrel. Joe is an agent for a company that produces the soft drink ‘Kolaloka’ and is trying to enforce the prohibition of alcohol. [SODA POP JOE’s] charm, bravura and humor ensured it 4.5 million viewers and the film is still regularly shown on Czech and Slovak TV stations.” –ROTTERDAM FILM FESTIVAL

title: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea (1916)(Silent with Live Music Score)
description: A groundbreaking underwater adventure based on the timeless Jules Verne tale! When a vessel investigating a monster terrorizing the seas is attacked, they’ll discover Captain Nemo and his fantastic submarine, the Nautilus. But the danger & mysteries deepen as Nemo’s backstory comes into focus.

title: Henry: Portrait Serial Killer
description: Forty years on, John McNaughton’s unflinching, profoundly bleak character study of an itinerant ex-con on a killing spree—loosely inspired by the real-life case of Henry Lee Lucas—has lost none of its power to shock, unsettle, and disturb.

title: The Off Hours
description: Vidiots is excited to welcome writer/director Megan Griffiths for a special 15th Anniversary screening of her engaging character study The Off Hours followed by a conversation with Griffiths and cast members Amy Seimetz , Scoot McNairy, and Ross Partridge , moderated by Vidiots Founding Member Mark Duplass!

title: COMANDANTE FRITZ
description: In this tongue-in-cheek comedy, East German Stasi officer Fritz travels to Cuba with orders to thwart a suspected CIA operation against Fidel Castro. In Havana he meets Lola, a young woman who changes the course of his life.

title: La Notte
description: Novelist Giovanni Pontano (Marcello Mastroianni) is the toast of the Italian literary scene, but smothered by the trappings of success. His misery weighs heavily on his wife, Lidia (Jeanne Moreau), already carrying her own cargo of existential anguish. In the course of a day and a night—spent at a hospital sickroom, a book launch, a nightclub, and a party at an industrialist’s villa, where Giovanni flirts extensively with the host’s daughter, Valentina (Monica Vitti)—the couple must come to terms with the extinction of the love that once existed between them… or not? A film steeped in despair but thrilling in its adventurous, architectonic use of the cinematic medium, from its opening credits—an avant-jazz/musique concrète overture accompanying the industrialized Milanese cityscape—to its beguiling final scene. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: The Invite
description: Does your summer need a little spice? Have we got the dinner party for you! Join us in the microcinema for Olivia Wilde’s wildly entertaining and perversely hilarious comedy The Invite for a fun and naughty night of indie cinema! Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down?

title: Les Bonnes Femmes
description: An early and enormous artistic triumph of the French New Wave, Chabrol’s quietly class-conscious film records the dreams, dramas, and self-deceptions of a quartet of young Parisian girls working at an appliance shop, among them Bernadette Lafont and Stéphane Audran. A study of the social habits of the petite bourgeoisie, set against indubitably authentic locations seen in crisp black-and-white courtesy DP Henri Decaë, which develops into a melancholy cautionary tale on the risks of romantic illusion. Part of Among Friends

title: TIME TO DIE / TIEMPO DE MORIR
description: Juan Sáyago returns to his hometown after serving 18 years in prison for the murder of Raúl Trueba. Although he killed in self-defense, rumors in town circulated during his absence speculating that the victim was killed in cold blood. Sáyago wants to rebuild the life he was denied with his old lover, Mariana Sampedro, but Trueba’s sons have sworn to avenge the murder of their father. This classic Mexican neo-western was the first realized screenplay of Nobel Prize winner Gabriel García Márquez and legendary Mexican novelist Carlos Fuentes. Under the direction of Arturo Ripstein, TIME TO DIE represents one of the earliest examples of New Mexican Cinema and one of the most accomplished Mexican films from the 1960s.

title: Superbuhei
description: A recovering alcoholic who spends his days tending bar inside a drab suburban supermarket begins to suspect he’s being stalked by his own evil twin in the mordant first feature from production designer-turned-director Josef Brandl.

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: The Hunger
description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit assistance from Susan Sarandon’s geriatrics researcher, then find themselves in a very, very attractive throuple. Yes, that’s “Bela Lugosi’s Dead” artists Bauhaus in a brief cameo. “Twenty years after Belle de Jour, Saint Laurent once again dressed Catherine Deneuve, for Tony Scott’s cult 1980s tale of elegant vampires. Her shoulder pads, lipstick, and veils defined an era.” —David Campany, Creative Director, International Center of Photography Part of Dressed by Yves Saint Laurent

title: Ponyo
description: Ponyo focuses on the friendship between 5-year-old Sosuke and a magical goldfish named Brunhilde, the young daughter of a sorcerer father and a sea-goddess mother. After wandering away from her father’s four-flippered submarine, Brunhilde washes ashore and is discovered by the curious Sosuke. Now renamed Ponyo, she forms a quick bond with Sosuke that fuels her yearning to be a real girl, and together they shoulder the cost of what that might take. The vibrant and colorful hand-drawn animations are a delight for audiences of all ages, as Hayao Miyazaki builds a world filled with magical goldfish, spellcasters, and sea goddesses in this tale of how friendships can blossom anywhere—even in the ocean’s depths.

title: Wendigo
description: Independent horror maestro Larry Fessenden returns to Scary Movies for a special 25th anniversary screening of his landmark 2001 chiller about a close-knit family’s encounter with vengeful forces of nature—human or otherwise—during a snowbound upstate vacation.

title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
description: Featuring a conversation with filmmaker Sasha Waters after the August 12th screening!

title: Cinematic Void Presents LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, THE FABULOUS STAINS
description: The media and disaffected teens mistake the acerbic rants of an obnoxious teenage punk rocker as a rallying cry for the women of America, launching her and her talentless group to national stardom.

title: Volver on 35mm
description: Join us for one of Pedro Almodóvar’s best dark comedies in all its colorful mastery in glorious 35mm film! From Academy Award-winner Pedro Almodóvar comes Volver , a darkly comedic and compassionate tribute to women and their resilience in the face of life’s most outrageous tribulations. A luminous Penélope Cruz leads an ensemble of gifted actresses, including Carmen Maura, star of Almodóvar’s Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown .

title: A Snake of June
description: Rinko Tatsumi (Asuka Kurosawa) is a suicide hotline worker resigned to a life of unhappiness until she receives a package from a blackmailer. Through the increasingly vulgar acts of exhibitionism her blackmailer forces upon her, she learns to shed the social restrictions and repression dominating her life. Shot on black-and-white film and tinted a monochromatic blue, Shinya Tsukamoto’s A Snake of June is a visual feast. Filled with shaky, hand-held camerawork, voyeuristic close-ups, and near-constant rain, Tsukamoto creates a damp and cold erotic thriller that explores sexual dynamics, transformation, and releasing one's inner desires.

title: The Thrill Killers             / Psychedelic Sexualis
description: Homicidal maniacs on a bloody rampage! In director Ray Dennis Steckler’s cult mindblower, a trio of psychotic killers escape from a mental institution and wreak havoc across Los Angeles. Liz Renay ( Desperate Living ), Steckler regular Carolyn Brandt, legendary stuntman Gary Kent, and Steckler himself (under his Cash Flagg alias) star.

title: Goody Goody
description: A mom-to-be’s stubborn conviction that she alone knows what’s best for her unborn child is put to the gruesomest of tests when alarming complications arise during a home delivery in director Raymond Creamer’s diabolical spin on prenatal horror.

title: Something Real
description: Adapted by screenwriter Martin Algus from his own 2018 novel, Evar Anvelt’s directorial debut is a pulse-pounding thriller pitting a porn-addicted family man against a hardened con artist whose seemingly foolproof blackmail scheme devolves into a dog-eat-dog fight for survival.

title: WHITE SUN OF THE DESERT / BELOE SOLNTSE PUSTYNI
description: “WHITE SUN OF THE DESERT is the final installment of what might be called a traditional Ostern. It tells the story of Fyodor Sukhov, a Red Army soldier in what would become the Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic. While clearly drawing on Western cinematic tropes, the film undoubtedly spoke to Soviet audiences regarding issues of nation and empire, reflecting the nationalist ideals of a Russian-dominated Central Asia. Over time, WHITE SUN OF THE DESERT achieved cult status in Russia and other post-Soviet countries. It’s famously watched by Russian cosmonauts before space missions as a good-luck tradition, underscoring its enduring cultural significance.” –PRINCETON

title: A TIME TO LOVE AND A TIME TO DIE
description: Private Ernst Graeber goes home to Germany on leave from the Eastern Front during World War II to visit his family, but Germany is no longer the same.

title: Welcome Space Brothers
description: The unbelievable but one-hundred percent true story of the Unarius Academy of Science —an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school in Southern California who in the 1980s became a prolific filmmaking collective and public access TV phenomenon under the direction of their outlandish spiritual leader Ruth E. Norman, AKA “Archangel Uriel.” Director Jodi Wille ( The Source Family ) brings this singular American story to the screen with the same wide-eyed fascination the subject demands. Engaging, enchanting, and extraterrestrial, Welcome Space Brothers is the most endearing cult documentary you’ve ever seen!

title: Ball of Fire             / The Lady Eve
description: Gary Cooper & Barbara Stanwyck star in a comedy classic from director Howard Hawks and screenwriters Charles Brackett and Billy Wilder!

title: ZACHARIAH
description: Firepower meets flower power in this outrageous western about two thrill-seeking cowboys who rock the range. Starring John Rubinstein (THE CAR), Don Johnson (TV’s MIAMI VICE), and Dick Van Patten (HIGH ANXIETY) and featuring legendary musicians Country Joe and the Fish and White Lightnin’, this psychedelic trip through the Wild West is an utterly unique film experience. Two cowboys (Rubinstein and Johnson) set out for adventure and join up with a band of rock ‘n’ roll outlaws. But as the two friends are seduced by their own quick-draw ambitions, a deadly rivalry grows between them, and they must struggle to find a path to peace – before they lose more than their reputations…and kill more than their friendship. Hollywood veteran George Englund (THE UGLY AMERICAN) directed this one-of-a-kind cult classic.

title: Bodyhackers
description: Cronenbergian body horror is deployed to darkly satirical ends in Carlos Conceição’s English-language debut, the noir-inflected story of an anti-corporate activist who becomes involved in a cult-like underworld of black-market plastic surgery.

title: Ponyo
description: Ponyo focuses on the friendship between 5-year-old Sosuke and a magical goldfish named Brunhilde, the young daughter of a sorcerer father and a sea-goddess mother.
